record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.context_brief: Average lower bounds for lattice point sets
record.original_question: For the d-dimensional lattice point set (({n a1/N}, ..., {n ad/N})) for n=0,1,...,N-1, prove an average-type lower bound showing that for every chi < 1 there is a constant C'_chi > 0 such that, for all N, the discrepancy D_N is at least C'_chi (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N for at least chi N^d choices of the integer vector (a1,...,ad) with 0 <= a1,...,ad < N.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Show that for every χ < 1 there is a constant C′χ > 0 such that for all N for the discrepancy DN of the lattice point set ... we have DN ≥ C′χ (log N)^(d−1) log log N / N for at least χN^d choices for (a1, . . . , ad) with 0 ≤ a1, . . . , ad < N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $N\ge 2$ and a vector $\mathbf{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_d)\in\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}^d$, consider the $d$-dimensional lattice point set
$$P_N(\mathbf{a})=\Big\{\Big(\Big\{\tfrac{n a_1}{N}\Big\},\dots,\Big\{\tfrac{n a_d}{N}\Big\}\Big):n=0,1,\dots,N-1\Big\}\subset[0,1)^d,$$
where $\{x\}=x-\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the fractional part. The (extreme/star) discrepancy of $P_N(\mathbf{a})$ is
$$D_N(\mathbf{a})=\sup_{B}\Big|\frac{\#\{0\le n<N:\,(\{n a_1/N\},\dots,\{n a_d/N\})\in B\}}{N}-\mathrm{vol}(B)\Big|,$$
where the supremum is taken over all axis-aligned boxes $B=\prod_{i=1}^d[\alpha_i,\beta_i)\subset[0,1)^d$.

Prove that for every $\chi<1$ there exists a constant $C'_\chi>0$ such that for every $N\ge 2$,
$$D_N(\mathbf{a})\;\ge\;C'_\chi\,\frac{(\log N)^{d-1}\log\log N}{N}$$
holds for at least $\chi N^d$ choices of $\mathbf{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_d)\in\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}^d$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source establishing the stated average-type lower bound $(\log N)^{d-1}\log\log N/N$ holding for a positive proportion $\chi N^d$ of lattice vectors $(a_1,\dots,a_d)$. Related metrical lower bounds for digital Kronecker-sequences and lattice point sets exist, but I could not verify a resolution of this specific quantitative average lower bound, so the status remains unclear.
